stateData.name: Utah
stateData.summary: Utah does not exempt Social Security outright — instead it offers a nonrefundable tax credit that offsets the tax owed. Below the income limit, the credit effectively zeroes out SS tax; above it, the credit phases out.
stateData.note: Frame this as a credit, not an exemption, in all content — the mechanism matters for accuracy even though the practical effect is similar for lower earners.

otherTaxingStates.name: Colorado
otherTaxingStates.summary: Fully exempt at age 65+. Ages 55-64 fully exempt if AGI is at or below the threshold; above it, only a partial deduction applies. Under 55, no special SS exemption.
otherTaxingStates.note: SB25-136 (effective Jan 1, 2026) also removed caps on the separate pension/annuity subtraction — mention this as a 2026-specific update.

otherTaxingStates.name: Connecticut
otherTaxingStates.summary: Fully exempt if AGI is at or below the threshold. Above it, no more than 25% of federally taxable benefits become subject to Connecticut tax.

otherTaxingStates.name: Minnesota
otherTaxingStates.summary: Fully exempt below the threshold; the exemption phases out gradually (10% reduction per $4,000 of income above the threshold) rather than disappearing all at once.
otherTaxingStates.note: 2025 figures cited across sources; confirm 2026 inflation-adjusted numbers before publishing.

seo.title: Is Social Security Taxed in Utah? (2026 Rules)
seo.description: Is Social Security taxed in Utah in 2026? Yes, but Utah offers a nonrefundable retirement tax credit to reduce or eliminate tax. See 2026 income caps.
